raw.markdown:
# Cholecystectomy Authorization Guide

## CPT Codes — Cholecystectomy

| CPT | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 47562 | Laparoscopic cholecystectomy | Standard laparoscopic cholecystectomy — most common approach |
| 47563 | Laparoscopic cholecystectomy with cholangiography | With intraoperative cholangiogram — add when CBD stones suspected |
| 47564 | Laparoscopic cholecystectomy with exploration of common duct | With laparoscopic CBD exploration |
| 47600 | Cholecystectomy | Open cholecystectomy |
| 47605 | Cholecystectomy; with cholangiography | Open with cholangiogram |
| 47610 | Cholecystectomy with exploration of common duct | Open with CBD exploration |
| 43239 | Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy including esophagus, stomach, and either the duodenum and/or jejunum as appropriate; with injection sclerosis of esophageal varices | ERCP for choledocholithiasis — often pre-operative |

## ICD-10 Codes

| ICD-10 | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| K80.20 | Calculus of gallbladder without cholecystitis, without obstruction | Symptomatic cholelithiasis — primary indication |
| K80.21 | Calculus of gallbladder without cholecystitis, with obstruction | Cholelithiasis with obstruction |
| K81.0 | Acute cholecystitis | Acute cholecystitis — urgent/semi-urgent indication |
| K81.1 | Chronic cholecystitis | Chronic cholecystitis |
| K82.0 | Obstruction of gallbladder | Gallbladder obstruction |
| K82.8 | Other specified diseases of gallbladder | Biliary dyskinesia, polyp, other |
| K80.40 | Calculus of bile duct without cholangitis or cholecystitis, without obstruction | Choledocholithiasis |
| K85.10 | Biliary acute pancreatitis without necrosis or infection | Gallstone pancreatitis — urgent indication |

## Payer Requirements

(Tabbed by payer: Medicare, Medicaid, Private)

### Medicare

**Required Documentation**
- Documented symptomatic cholelithiasis confirmed by ultrasound or other imaging
- Clinical documentation of biliary colic, acute cholecystitis, or other biliary complication
- Surgeon documentation of indication for cholecystectomy
- ASA classification and surgical risk assessment

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- ✓ Symptomatic cholelithiasis with documented biliary colic, nausea, or fatty food intolerance
- ✓ Acute or chronic cholecystitis
- ✓ Choledocholithiasis or gallstone pancreatitis
- ✓ Biliary dyskinesia with ejection fraction <35% on HIDA scan
- ✓ Gallbladder polyp ≥10mm

**Reimbursement Note**
Medicare covers elective cholecystectomy for symptomatic cholelithiasis without requiring a specific number of prior conservative treatment attempts. Acute cholecystitis is covered as urgent/semi-urgent. Laparoscopic approach (47562) is preferred and reimbursed at standard rates.

**Known Payer Policies**
- [Covered] Medicare (CMS): Covered for symptomatic cholelithiasis, acute cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis, gallstone pancreatitis; no mandatory conservative treatment period

### Medicaid

**Required Documentation**
- Prior authorization may be required depending on state
- Documented symptomatic cholelithiasis on imaging
- Clinical documentation of symptoms

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- ✓ Symptomatic cholelithiasis with imaging confirmation
- ✓ Acute cholecystitis
- ✓ Biliary complications

**Reimbursement Note**
Medicaid coverage for elective cholecystectomy is generally available in most states for symptomatic disease. Prior authorization requirements vary by state. Acute cholecystitis is typically covered without prior authorization.

**Known Payer Policies**
- [Covered] Medicaid (state-specific): Generally covered for symptomatic disease; prior auth requirements vary by state

### Private

**Required Documentation**
- Prior authorization required by most commercial payers for elective cholecystectomy
- Ultrasound or imaging confirming cholelithiasis or biliary pathology
- Documentation of symptomatic disease (biliary colic, nausea, fatty food intolerance)
- Duration and frequency of symptoms
- For biliary dyskinesia: HIDA scan with ejection fraction <35%
- For gallbladder polyp: imaging documentation of polyp size ≥10mm
- Conservative treatment documentation (dietary modification) — some payers require

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- ✓ Symptomatic cholelithiasis with ≥2 episodes of biliary colic OR daily symptoms
- ✓ Acute or chronic cholecystitis
- ✓ Choledocholithiasis or gallstone pancreatitis
- ✓ Biliary dyskinesia (HIDA EF <35%) with symptoms
- ✓ Gallbladder polyp ≥10mm (malignancy risk)

**Reimbursement Note**
Most commercial payers cover elective cholecystectomy for symptomatic cholelithiasis without requiring a mandatory conservative treatment period. Document symptom frequency and severity. For biliary dyskinesia, HIDA scan with EF <35% is required. Acute cholecystitis is typically covered without prior authorization.

**Known Payer Policies**
- [Covered] UnitedHealthcare: Covers symptomatic cholelithiasis; imaging required; biliary dyskinesia requires HIDA EF <35%
- [Covered] Aetna: Covers symptomatic cholelithiasis with imaging; acute cholecystitis covered urgently
- [Covered] Cigna: Covers for symptomatic disease; documentation of symptoms and imaging required
- [Covered] Anthem/BCBS: Covers symptomatic cholelithiasis; prior auth required for elective cases
- [Covered] Humana: Covers per standard surgical criteria; imaging confirmation required
